say: Today: XGBoost. The idea is simple. Many small trees, built one after another.

actions.text: XGBoost = many small trees, in a row

say: We start with the data and a first tree. It makes a rough guess.
The guess is wrong by some amount. We call that the residual, the mistake that is left.
Here is the key trick. Tree 2 does not learn y. It learns only the mistakes of tree 1.
Repeat this many times. Each tree fixes what is still wrong.
The final prediction is the sum of all trees, each one scaled down by a small learning rate.
What makes it extreme? A penalty on tree size, so trees stay small and do not overfit.

actions.text: loss + Ω(tree)  ← penalty on leaves & weights

say: Interview tip: be ready to explain why boosting reduces bias, while bagging like random forest reduces variance.

actions.text:
Interview tip:
boosting → less bias
bagging → less variance
